Read the requirement file: /workspace/requirements/datazoom-single-point-position.yaml

Your job is READ-ONLY research. Do NOT edit any files. Produce a precise, actionable implementation plan that another engineer can execute without re-reading the whole codebase.

Method:
1. Read the requirement yaml fully.
2. Use grep/glob/read to locate the exact source files, functions, and line numbers involved. Be thorough - search src/, test/, index.d.ts, package.json, build/, theme/ as relevant.
3. Read enough surrounding code to understand the current behavior and precisely what must change.
4. Check /workspace/test/ut/spec for existing unit tests that cover this area (they tell you the expected API shape).
5. Note the exact current code that must be replaced (quote it) and what the replacement should be.

Be specific: file path + line numbers + current code snippet + intended new code. If the requirement implies a new public option, name the option, its type location in the *Option interfaces, and the default value.

Return the structured plan.

Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). 2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  When a chart has only one data point, the slider dataZoom can compute the wrong position and render in the wrong place, which makes simple charts look broken.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Slider dataZoom should place itself correctly even when the controlled series contains just a single point.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  A one-point chart shows the dataZoom in the expected location instead of offsetting it because of invalid geometry calculations.
14	
15	  '

content.text:
I confirmed the root cause empirically by running the real chart in a scratch jest harness (all scratch files were created and removed under `/tmp`; nothing in the repo was modified).

**Reproduced:** 500×400 chart, `xAxis: {type: 'time'}`, `dataZoom: [{type:'slider'}]`, `series: [{type:'line', data: [[1700000000000, 10]]}]` →
- `sliderView.group.x === NaN` (correct value is `77.8`, which is what the same chart yields with 2 points, or with a `category`/`value` axis)
- `_shadowPolygonPts === [[375,0],[0,0],[NaN,15]]`

**Verified fix:** guarding the zero-span division at `SliderZoomView.ts:394` restores `group.x === 77.79999995231628` and `_shadowPolygonPts === [[375,0],[0,0],[0,15]]`, byte-identical to the healthy multi-point / category / value cases.

input.summary: The slider dataZoom renders at an invalid (NaN) position when the data-shadow series has a degenerate value extent on a time axis — most commonly a series with a single data point. `SliderZoomView._renderDataShadow` divides by `thisDataExtent[1] - thisDataExtent[0]`, which is `0` for one point, producing `Infinity`, then `0 * Infinity = NaN` for the shadow x-coordinate; the NaN flows into the polygon/polyline points, into the group bounding rect, and finally into `this.group.x`. Guard the division so a zero span maps the point to coordinate `0`, matching what category/value axes already do.
steps:
PRIMARY FIX — /workspace/src/component/dataZoom/SliderZoomView.ts, method `_renderDataShadow` (declared at line 351; the affected block is inside the `if (data !== this._shadowData || ...)` guard starting at line 376).

Replace line 394, currently exactly:
```ts
            const normalizationConstant = size[0] / (thisDataExtent[1] - thisDataExtent[0]);
```
with a zero-span guard:
```ts
            // When every value on this axis is identical (e.g. the series has only
            // one data point), the extent span is 0 and this division yields
            // Infinity. `thisCoord` below then becomes 0 * Infinity === NaN, which
            // propagates into the data-shadow polygon/polyline points, into
            // `_positionGroup`'s bounding rect, and finally into `this.group.x`,
            // rendering the whole slider at an invalid position. See #single-point.
            const thisDataSpan = thisDataExtent[1] - thisDataExtent[0];
            const normalizationConstant = thisDataSpan === 0 ? 0 : size[0] / thisDataSpan;
```
Do NOT gate on `data.count() === 1`; gate on the span, because N points that all share the same time value hit the identical divide-by-zero.

Surrounding context for orientation (lines 380-396, unchanged apart from 394):
```ts
            const thisDataExtent = data.getDataExtent(info.thisDim);   // 380
            ...
            const step = thisShadowExtent[1] / (Math.max(1, data.count() - 1)); // 393
            const normalizationConstant = size[0] / (thisDataExtent[1] - thisDataExtent[0]); // 394  <-- BUG
            const isTimeAxis = info.thisAxis.type === 'time';          // 395
            let thisCoord = -step;                                     // 396
```
The NaN is produced at lines 410-411:
```ts
                thisCoord = isTimeAxis
                    ? (+thisValue - thisDataExtent[0]) * normalizationConstant
```
With the guard, `thisCoord` becomes `0`, which is exactly the value the non-time branch (`thisCoord + step`, i.e. `-size[0] + size[0]`) already produces for a one-point series — so time and non-time axes stay consistent.

VERIFIED BEHAVIOUR (measured, not assumed). Chart 500x400, `xAxis: {type:'time'}`, `yAxis: {}`, `dataZoom: [{type:'slider'}]`, `series: [{type:'line', data: [[1700000000000, 10]]}]`.
  - BEFORE the fix: `sliderView.group.x === NaN`, `sliderView._shadowPolygonPts === [[375,0],[0,0],[NaN,15]]`.
  - AFTER the fix: `sliderView.group.x === 77.79999995231628`, `_shadowPolygonPts === [[375,0],[0,0],[0,15]]`.
  - Control cases already correct before and unchanged after: time axis with 2 points, `category` axis with 1 point, `value` axis with 1 point — all `group.x === 77.79999995231628`.
Use these exact numbers as the regression assertions.

OPTIONAL VISUAL TEST CASE — /workspace/test/ already has 28 `dataZoom-*.html` files. Add `/workspace/test/dataZoom-single-data.html` following the structure of `/workspace/test/dataZoom-timeAxis.html` (Apache HTML comment license header lines 2-18, the `lib/simpleRequire.js` / `lib/config.js` / `lib/jquery.min.js` / `lib/facePrint.js` / `lib/testHelper.js` script tags, `lib/reset.css`, a `<div id="main0">` and a `require(['echarts'], function (echarts) { ... testHelper.create(echarts, 'main0', {...}) })` block). Chart it with `xAxis: {type:'time'}`, a single `[timestamp, value]` datum, and `dataZoom: [{type:'slider'}]`, titled to say the slider must sit under the grid rather than disappear. Purely for the visual-regression suite; skip if the task scope is source-only.

NO NEW PUBLIC OPTION is implied by this requirement. Do not touch `src/component/dataZoom/SliderZoomModel.ts` (the `SliderDataZoomOption` interface), `index.d.ts`, `src/export/*`, or any theme/build file. The change is a pure internal numeric guard.
input.risks:
Scope/ambiguity: the requirement says "only one data point" generally, but only the TIME-axis path is actually broken — `category` and `value` x-axes with one point already position correctly (measured `group.x === 77.8` for both). Do not "fix" the non-time branch; `step = thisShadowExtent[1] / Math.max(1, data.count() - 1)` at line 393 is already guarded by `Math.max(1, ...)`.

Trigger is broader than the title: any series whose data-shadow dimension has a zero-width extent on a time axis (N points all sharing one timestamp) hits the same divide-by-zero. Gate the fix on the span being 0, not on `data.count() === 1`, or the broader case stays broken.

Shared code touched by other requirements: `SliderZoomView.ts` is also the target of `slider-handlelabel-optional.yaml` (which touches `_renderHandle` around lines 636-651 and `_showDataInfo` at 906-923) and of anything touching `_updateDataInfo`. This fix only edits line 394 inside `_renderDataShadow`, so there is no textual overlap — but expect merge adjacency if both land in the same branch.

Choice of fallback value: mapping a zero-span extent to coordinate `0` (rather than `size[0] / 2`, i.e. centering the point) was chosen because it exactly reproduces what the existing non-time branch already yields for a one-point series, keeping time and category/value axes visually identical. If a reviewer prefers the shadow point centered, that would be a deliberate behaviour change for ALL axis types, not just this guard.

`_positionGroup` (lines 296-299) remains structurally fragile: any future NaN in child geometry still poisons `this.group.x` silently via zrender's `BoundingRect.union` (`Math.min`/`Math.max` propagate NaN). Listed as optional hardening; not needed for the acceptance signal.
